I don't get the overwhelmingly positive rating for this one. It's... fine, but that's it. The "teeth" which are basically the artifacts or passives, are... well, just small % changes that compound. The items are fine. You can interact with the shopkeeper and there are some neat easter eggs but that's... about it. I don't see any depth so far, it's pretty much a casino with not a lot of content and the characters are wildly imbalanced. The enemies who are supposed to switch sides every other turn only work half the runs (and maybe that's on purpose too?). Again, not a bad game, but the overwhelmingly positiive rating there is VERY deceptive. The game is just OK, I'd strongly suggest waiting a few good more months before spending money here. I'll check back later to see what is added since it's too late for me to get a refund myself.

[h2]Sol Cesto te garde.[/h2] Every choice feels wrong - [i]and I keep going anyway.[/i] The art pulls me in. The music won’t leave me alone. [b]The gameplay drives me mad.[/b] It feels like a joke. [i]A cruel one.[/i] [b]And I’m still laughing.[/b] https://youtu.be/BChCvZGQhlA?si=tYM3mSr1dZ3kD3o7

Sol Cesto doesn't currently have enough content to be worth the asking price, even with a discount. I finished all available content in 3h, ending with an anticlimactic screen showing there is no more content past the third floor. This game has massive potential to be good - with more variety of enemies, bosses, and teeth, it would feel less same-y after a few hours. Currently, the amount of content in the paid version is more equivalent to a demo than being a full game, so I can't recommend picking this up until significantly more content is added.

这名字也太整蛊了 盐面团 我百度了一下 这游戏那几个英文字母是葡萄牙语 sol是太阳，cesto是道路，不知道为啥合到一起翻译sol cesto 就变成盐面团了（葡萄牙语很神奇吧） 明明游戏内的翻译都没有不通顺的地方，为啥游戏的名字确实机翻的？很神秘 感觉应该叫 寻日之路、《重生之成为下楼勇士却无法选定下楼位置特殊能力是拔牙是否搞错了什么》、[spoiler]下一百层找日[/spoiler]之类的大伙才有点进来的可能

The biggest problem with this game and it shares this with other rougelikes is after playing a few games you begin to recognize when a given run is pointless. Unless you get the right buffs at the right time then depending on your character there's just no point continuing a run. Also, depending on the character you play, even the first screen can be stupidly punishing so you might find yourself just noping out before you even make a first move depending on the RNG. On top of that there are some basic QoL issues that seem to remain here. Things like the game not respecting your settings - music is on even though music is at 0 volume, game is full screen even though full screen was unchecked last time you played and the worst one, starting a game to find a setting wrong only to find you have to quit your run just to reset the settings you already set because the game won't let you change settings without quitting. Overall I found the game a bit of a let down. There's so many complete, playable games out there. I'd recommend trying something else unless the art style here really appeals to you.

为啥改名了，我感觉原来的《盐面团》更好听，首发就买了，画风很独特，然后当时流程比较短，而且我竟然从一个rogue游戏玩出了打击感，好评！！

《寻日之旅》是一款随机性相当高的肉鸽游戏，游戏原名《盐面团》，现在改名为《寻日之旅》，游戏仍处于EA阶段，不过质量过硬，玩起来十分上头。 游戏玩法简单，地下城的每个关卡都由4 x 4的格子组成，格子里有怪物、陷阱、宝箱或回血道具。玩家没办法自由选择打开哪个格子，只能选择其中某一行，角色会按照概率随机打开这一行的1个格子。 游戏拥有全局升级系统，前期缺乏升级时角色的数值很低，会很容易被小怪群殴死。因此玩家前期经常要面临抉择，是否要赌概率去拿宝箱/回血道具，赌赢了能愉快地增加资源，赌输了就会被怪物打掉血，非常考验玩家的心态和策略。 总的来说，《寻日之旅》是一款质量优秀、价格合理、物超所值的肉鸽游戏，推荐喜欢肉鸽游戏的玩家入手。 [table][td]欢迎关注鉴赏家[url= https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45519015/]“无趣评测”[/url][/td][/table]

I think the game itself is well made and enjoyable. I don't recommend for players like me who already had most/all of the game unlocked in early access. Giving us 1500 gold doesn't come even close to making up for what myself and others already had unlocked and you are making us unlock all the characters over again. Deleting our saves and making us start from scratch feels bad and like a forced grind. If players want to start a fresh game on a new save file give them that option but let us keep what we had.

They wiped my save without warning and gave me a fraction of the gold needed to unlock what I had lost. Wont be grinding it out again. Too many indie rogue likes out there for me to tolerate that kinda crap with my time.

Edit after completing the game to 100%, scroll down for the end thoughts: ----- Original Statement ----- This game had potential to be good, it really did... But it's been left at a state that just makes this game badly unfair rather than fun random. It constantly punishes you for trying to play the game and wanting to have fun, leading you to restart the first screen until you can get anywhere to a managable position, sometimes the randomness feels so unbalanced that there are people reporting of having rooms filled with just traps, making it near impossible. Here are my gripes with the game that would make it more fun: There was a segment about the blacksmith but I removed it because it kinda sucked so I'd propose to give him a little earlier on the third section. Give player a healing option if their health is 1-2. Having a strawberry available if the player has low enough health could help the player in a pinch, even if the chances of landing on one are still random, at least it would give you an option to heal up and not just die. Adjust the randomness to the character being played. The major issue with the game is how it will more often than not, throw you in a near impossible room that can just straight up kill you rather than give you a logical challenge to solve. More often than not it's not a case of "Do you land here for a reward or take the safer option", no, most of the time it's "Here's a room full of enemies that will deal a bunch of damage to you, screw you". If any issues get adressed and made better, I will change the review or update it but for now... I cannot recommend the game, it has amazing art style and wonderful soundtrack but that's all this game offers, the gameplay is just so bad that you're better off paying the creator to draw you something than playing this mess. I already sunk a lot of time in it and will continue but so far, it's just not good. ----- After beating the game to 100% ----- So despite my issues I persevered and... I still don't like it. Yeah, I've done everything in the game that there is and I still have hard time recommend it. If you want an unfairly challenging game, you should for sure buy it but I feel like this game at some point becomes less about thinking and strategising and becomes more of a "Don't think, just do it" type of game because of course it will kick you in the nuts, you just gotta accept it will do and eventually it will let you beat it.

这个游戏数值很简陋，就战斗部分来说没有什么策略， 但是以下是一些隐藏要素。我知道你们也懒得翻社区，翻指南。有些是我搬的，有些是我试出来的。 你要是不喜欢剧透 就应该跳过这个评测： 0.多语言选择时，应该是作者自己录的，不同语言的“早上好”。byd怎么还把自己录笑了。 [spoiler] 1.拽商人的鼻子会让他眩晕，可以偷一个物品。后续可以用锤子或弹弓击晕，每次也是摸一个物品[/spoiler] [spoiler] 2.商人的桌子上有闪光甲虫，点掉甲虫就给1块钱，后续可以解锁一个牙齿，点掉甲虫给更多钱。[/spoiler] [spoiler] 3.向商人使用武器，是地牢游戏不得不品鉴的一个传统。杀死商人后，清图蹦出来的也变成骷髅脸了。细节呀。[/spoiler] [spoiler] 4.在迷宫的4*4关卡界面，有时候ui边框会出现一个哥布林，点掉它给钱，点40次可以解锁。[/spoiler] [spoiler] 5.在井的墙壁上有时会有金色砖块，点掉后出现暗格，内含道具、回血或钱。[/spoiler] [spoiler] 6. 骰子可以用在其他界面来刷新物品，例如商城。[/spoiler] [spoiler] 7. 石质雕像可以用炸弹或锤子炸掉另一个角，获得一个随机道具。注意集束炸弹没有用。[/spoiler] 长笛是在井水里捞部件解锁的，解锁长笛后，注意音符短按和长按是不同的效果。笛子一局只能用一次。 [spoiler] a.商人打折曲：蓝 红 长黄 长蓝 长黄。这个组合就是游戏steam页面那个gif,作者告诉你的。[/spoiler] [spoiler] b.送币回家曲：长红 长红 红 蓝 黄。这个组合通过商店里买一个音乐盒获得。[/spoiler] [spoiler] c.吹了回血曲：长黄 红 蓝 长红 长蓝。这个组合通过在泉水页面使用冰块获得。[/spoiler] [spoiler] d.物法交换曲：蓝 长红 蓝 长红 黄。这个组合通过在铁匠页面使用蜡烛获得。[/spoiler]

I do not recommend rougelikes that don't let you save & quit mid-run out of principle. Nobody likes to have to end their god run because of sudden irl obligations. 极吃运气的概率游戏。 我理解大量策略游戏都会在某个节点因为运气原因败北，但是这个游戏因为运气败北带来的体验是极端负面的。 其一，游戏游玩过程就是直观的概率结果展示，你选择一排，根据不同分类几率随机落入某个格中达成效果。后期可以通过改变某个分类的几率、删除某个地块的内容、使用道具跳过选择、使用技能等方法直接达成有利结果，但许多时候即使到最后期你也无可避免的要面临概率的审判，不论你的构筑有多好。 其二，我是真的讨厌你的陷阱设计，可以重复落入不会消失，多数是落入多次即斩杀，甚至有的还限制了显示时间抉择。除了特定道具可以削除，陷阱在大多数时候都是看了鬼见愁的内容。配合构筑和负面影响，陷阱是永远过不去的绊脚石。 其三，局外升级肝进度。本作局内局外共用统一货币，局内特定关卡可以上交货币交回局外，局外内容又多升级需求又大单个提升又小，我觉得没有考虑到玩家接受度和肝度。 本作对我的优点在于初见的新鲜度+各种知识小技巧提升游戏乐趣+美术。 我能理解制作组想要做的局内局外资源抉择+行差踏错一步的走钢丝策略乐趣，但是这反映到游戏内就表现为放大你投出失败结果的挫折感，中等不推荐。
美术风格很吸引人，学会套路之后难度不算高，就是一把流程比较长一旦中后期翻车会很痛苦，有些地方随机性太大不太可控，总体体验还不错

讲一个故事：寻日之旅（Sol Cesto） 这个世界的太阳在某天消失了，有人目击到太阳飞进了一个地牢深处。在这样一个世界枯萎终日无光的背景下，吸引来各种身份背景的人自发深入寻找太阳。 在这些人中，有着肩负使命的骑士，神通广大的巫师，断臂失去一切只剩复仇的战士，不远万里前来的猎人。还有被视作全村希望，虽满心恐惧，但为了拯救同胞前来的农夫。 探寻的动静也吸引了吸血鬼和蜥蜴的注意，一位能吸引一切形式的生命力，不知疲倦地追逐太阳；一位只会发出阵阵嘶嘶声，受伤还会断尾逃跑。以上是可以使用的角色，每一位都有着各自的特长技能或优质属性，除了农夫，他没有特殊能力，属性也最低，好在出发时亲朋好友给他多塞了些道具。 后来在经历各种艰难险阻，一次次的尝试后他们终于见到了太阳并迎来他们的结局：骑士将太阳献给了国王。巫师将太阳锁在塔顶，终日凝望。猎人盗走了这个世界的太阳，将太阳射向了自己的世界。（是的，后来我才知道猎人是联动角色）战士将太阳筑成了新手臂，带着这份强大的力量寻找仇敌。吸血鬼将太阳抱入怀中，身体越是焚烧双手越是紧握，直到发出最后一声喘息，灰飞烟灭。蜥蜴抓住太阳往更深处挖掘，在接近地球核心的地方，蜥蜴簇拥着太阳不停筑巢，下蛋，等着蛋中蜥蜴破土而出。。。终结人类的时代。太阳的力量太强大了，勾引着人内心的欲望，这份力量也在扭曲着所拥有者。 但是，有一个人物不一样。没有技能的农夫，他不需要太阳之力。使用农夫通关是个比较困难的过程，必须攒下所有钱购买物品，尽可能多地拖延回合。令我喜欢这个角色的一个原因是：当他濒临死亡时，脑海中会闪过亲朋好友和他妻子的画面，这份决心让他拥有了重新爬起的力量。（是的，他是唯一一个自带复活一次的角色）终于，农夫见到了太阳，将太阳还给了世界。 让我感动的，一是他倒地时的重新站起，二是再次睁开眼，发现自己躺在外面，笑着流出的那份泪。看着农夫的结局，看着他躺在草地，眼中是一望无际的碧蓝色，不由得鼻尖一酸。这也是我想去分享这个故事的起因，当其他强者在靠“向外索取”获得力量时，这个最弱小的农夫选择了“向内扎根”。濒死时脑中闪过的，不是“我要拯救这个世界”，不是“我要获得力量”，而是那些最琐碎，最平凡的日常。我喜欢这份“为了回家而站起来”的决心，它不再是少数英雄的专利，而是每一个普通人都拥有的铠甲。 回看整个寻日之旅，说是寻日，实则是一场太阳的掠夺战。所有强大的角色，都把太阳当成了一件可以被占有、被利用、被交易的物品。他们都在追逐太阳的附加价值，却忘了太阳最本来的样子。反而农夫他不需要太阳的力量。他想要的，从来都只是太阳本身——是能让麦子成熟的阳光，是能让花儿开放的温暖，是能让孩子们在田野里奔跑的光明。 最后是农夫结局画面的一些讨论：我想这个画面之所以有这么大的力量，是因为它没有任何多余的东西。没有欢呼的人群，没有加冕的仪式，没有记者的采访，没有刻着他名字的纪念碑。甚至没有人知道，是这个不起眼的农夫，把太阳带了回来。世界恢复了原样，就好像什么都没有发生过一样。枯萎的草木重新发芽，冰封的河流开始解冻，孩子们跑出家门欢呼雀跃，而农夫，只是拍了拍身上的泥土，朝着村子的方向走去。。。（写到这鼻子又酸了） 好了，就到这，感谢阅读。 Tell a story: The Journey to Find the Sun (Sol Cesto) One day, the sun of this world vanished, witnessed flying deep into a dungeon. Against a backdrop of a world withering in perpetual darkness, people from all walks of life spontaneously set out on a quest to find the sun. Among them are a knight burdened with a sacred mission, a wizard of immense magical power, a warrior who lost his arm and everything else, driven solely by vengeance, and a hunter who traveled thousands of miles to join the quest. There is also a farmer, seen as the village's last hope, trembling with fear yet determined to save his people. Their movements attract the attention of both vampires and lizards—one capable of drawing in all forms of life energy, tirelessly chasing the sun; the other making only hissing sounds, fleeing with its tail severed when injured. These are the playable characters, each possessing unique skills or superior attributes. The farmer stands apart—lacking special abilities and having the lowest stats—but fortunately, friends and family packed him extra items before departure. Later, after enduring countless hardships and repeated attempts, they finally beheld the sun and met their fates: the knight offered the sun to the king; the wizard locked it atop a tower, gazing at it endlessly; the hunter stole the world's sun and shot it toward his own realm. (Yes, only later did I learn that the hunter was a crossover character.) The warrior forged the sun into a new arm, wielding its immense power in search of vengeance. The vampire embraced the sun, clutching it tighter as his body burned, until his final breath escaped and he turned to ashes. The lizard seized the sun and burrowed deeper, gathering around it near Earth's core, building nests, laying eggs, waiting for the lizards within to hatch and break through the earth—ushering in the end of humanity. The sun's power is too great, tempting the deepest desires within people, warping those who possess it. But there is one character who stands apart. The farmer, lacking any special skills, does not need the power of the sun. Clearing the game as the farmer is a challenging process—requiring you to save every penny to buy items and stretch each turn as long as possible. One reason I love this character is that when he's on the verge of death, images of his loved ones and his wife flash through his mind, giving him the strength to rise again. (Yes, he's the only character who can revive once.) Finally, the farmer sees the sun—and returns it to the world. What moved me was first his rising again after falling, and second, the tears that streamed as he opened his eyes once more, realizing he lay outside—smiling. Watching the farmer's fate, seeing him lying on the grass with endless emerald blue stretching before his eyes, I couldn't help but feel a lump in my throat. This is why I wanted to share this story: while other strong ones gain power by "taking from the outside," this weakest of farmers chose to "take root within." In his final moments, what flashed through his mind wasn't "I must save the world" or "I must gain strength," but rather those most ordinary, mundane daily moments. I love this determination—to rise up simply to return home. It's no longer the privilege of a few heroes, but the armor every ordinary person can wear. Looking back on the entire journey to find the sun, what we call a search for the sun is actually a battle of plundering it. All the powerful characters treat the sun as an object to be possessed, exploited, and traded. They chase after its added value, forgetting the sun's true essence. In contrast, the farmer does not need the sun's power. What he has always wanted is simply the sun itself—the sunlight that ripens wheat, the warmth that makes flowers bloom, the light that allows children to run freely across the fields. Finally, some thoughts on the farmer's ending scene: I think this image carries such powerful impact precisely because it contains nothing superfluous—no cheering crowds, no coronation ceremony, no interviews with journalists, no monument bearing his name. Not even anyone knows that it was this unremarkable farmer who brought the sun back. The world simply returns to normal, as if nothing had happened at all. Withered plants sprout anew, frozen rivers begin to thaw, children rush out of their homes in joy, while the farmer merely shakes the dirt from his clothes and walks toward the village... (Writing this makes my nose tingle again.) Alright, that's it. Thank you for reading.

Man, I really loved this game, then I liked this game, and now I kind of hate it. The beggining is fantastic. I love the theme and the art style. The mechanics are also innovative and interesting, while remaining familiar enough to be comfortable to learn. Then, the mid-game hits, where you unlocked most of the stuff and most characters and are now getting more familiar with the game loop. That's when you start noticing the little annoyances: [list] [*]The fact that the animations are unskippable, so every time you click on a row, the camera zooms-in, shows the animation of the cell you got, and zooms-out. This also applies to other animations, like the floor clear animation, or the boss intros and outros. [*]The fact that even if the whole floor is beatable with your base stats and no damage taken, you have to manually pick each row 4 times and watch the whole animation every time to get the chests/floor clear. [*]The fact that many of the items and power-ups are garbage and should be rerolled every time you encounter them. [*]The barebones options menu [*]The fact that money just loses all meaning in the mid-game, because you already have all the permanent upgrades, so the whole money-retrieving system just makes no sense anymore, pads out your runs and adds unnecessary clutter. [*]And each run takes around 30-45 minutes, but 80% of the runtime is just tedious. There isn't enough enemy/environment variety to make them interesting. The biomes play-out exactly the same each time. [/list] And then, the cherry on top. (Spoilers for the "end-game", even though I haven't finished the game as I got too bored to do it.) [spoiler] It turns out, that to progress and, I'm guessing, get to the ending, you have to get through the whole game 4 more times, while collecting a different gem in each of the biomes to open the next gate. [/spoiler] Brother... You couldn't think of a less engaging progress-lock if you tried. I got around half-way there and just gave up. The runs take too much time, are too similar to each other from the lack of variety, and are extremely punishing (especially in the last biome). You can slog through the first 3 biomes for 40 minutes, and then get unlucky with 3 rooms in a row in the fourth biome, and get reset. And honestly, 90% of this wouldn't be a problem, if only there was an option to skip the cell-picking and floor-changing animations. Then the runs wouldn't feel as boring, because you could just click through them a lot faster. There's nothing entertaining in clicking through the first 2 biomes on autopilot every time in the run. I hope they add some QoL features, because with some improvements, this would be a really good game. As of right now, the end-game feels very cheap and the UX is quite poor after a few hours.

I am writing this to collect my thoughts after 100% completing this charming, fun and frustrating game. I beat the game with all characters and got all achievements after slightly under 30 hours. I think I spent about 10 hours unlocking the most important unlocks, and then the rest on finding the secrets and figuring out how to consistently beat the game with all characters. In the end, I find the game has nothing more to offer after that. This compares poorly to something like Slay the Spire, which takes like 100+ hours to get all the achievements, and is still highly playable after that (over 1400 hours at the time of writing). I have two points related to this that I want to expand on. My first point, and my main complaint about the game (as with every game that implements this mechanic), is the meta unlock/upgrade system. I really wish developers would stop implementing this. In Sol Cesto this problem is exaggerated by the fact that unlocks are made by setting aside currency you earn throughout the run, that you would ohterwise use to buy items that are essential to beating the run. In theory there might be an interesting decision of whether to spend gold on items or save it for upgrades. But because a lot of upgrades are pretty essential to beating the game, you really do not have a choice. If you spend your gold on items, you are probably going to lose your run anyways with nothing to show for it. So this leads to about 10 hours of (mostly) grinding to unlock the actual game. There are so many other problems with this system, but the bottom line is that the game: -does not reward actual run progress -has a wonky difficulty curve My second point is that of replayability. I am not quite sure whether the game is not deep enough, or if it is just poorly balanced. Regardless, the game ends up having a very dominant strategy that allows you to consistently win with every character. This completely diminishes the interest in replaying the game after beating it. While it was fun figuring out and executing this strategy, every run feels the same once you figure it out. Apart from these two points, the game mostly holds up for the amount of time it lasts. Would I recommend the game? If you expect a highly replayable game where you do not have to go through a bunch of grinding just to unlock the full game, then no. But if you just want a small, interesting challenge with an uncanny atmosphere, and can forgive the developers for wasting your time unlocking its features, I will absolutely recommend it.

Sol Cesto is honestly a great, unique experience, especially if you like playing with odds in games, and I enjoyed playing the game to 100% completion, but after I did so, I couldn't help but notice things. For one, balancing. I think it's obvious this game was made more in favor for strength rather than magic. Granted, more magic aligned monsters have special abilities that can affect how you approach any given room, but generally, it feels much better to upgrade your strength every time unless you either already have more magic than strength, or your teeth RNG just so happens to make it necessary. Another thing is the items. Most of them suck unfortunately. The throwing stars, while being able to hit more than one monster on the same line, is outclassed by the guaranteed four kills (or however many lines with at least one monster on them) the scatter bombs give you. The egg is a potion reskin from the start with its only real function being that it unlocks the lizard (a pretty underwhelming unlock). The power potion, giving you +3/+3 at most for one turn is completely invalidated by the bubble shield that lasts as long as you don't hit a monster, and allows you to one-shot anything. The spider web is only useful for progression and I suppose the 5,000G achievement, but when you have done those, it's completely useless. A pretty good chunk of items in the game pollute the shop item pool, and really, could have been thought out better. Same thing goes for the the source items. Sharp Sword is usually not worth taking over the potential alternatives you could get, the bird is never worth getting, period, and the gold pouch, while it can maybe help you for a trip to the shop once, maybe twice if your rng is good, lacks the staying power of the other items you could get There are some bugs in the game, obviously. Nothing terrible, but sometimes its just a bit irking. Sometimes you'd click on a line and it would zoom in, but you never moved, sometimes monsters whose abilities depend on the player's moves don't do anything and end up screwing up your flow (the switching rabbit especially). There's a bug where if you pick the golden dentures, it gives you the bottom denture first and then gives you it again the next time you pick the dentures. Again, nothing terrible, and can be overlooked, but when it happens, I can't help but notice it. Then there's bosses. The first boss is well done, it's easy but high stakes, I have no problems there. The second boss, while he can be tricky and sort of annoying, isn't really a difficult boss, only dealing one damage if you get caught in his web. He can get you good if you land on a high stat monster on a web, but that's not usually a death sentence. The third boss is even worse. Unless you happen to get a lot of black holes, you will survive this guy. He doesn't deal damage directly, the vertical path can be easily avoided via blank spaces, and more often than not, I land either on a safe monster or even a bonus tile. The fourth boss is seemingly missing from the game, which is disappointing given the biome it would have been in. The REAL fourth boss had disappointed me since I first saw it, it being a reskin of the first boss with one new attack that only deals one damage. The first boss is very easy, but it at the very least has some meaningful stakes, that being you instantly die if you get in range of its mouth. The second and third boss are easier than a bad RNG room most of the time, and the fourth boss is only really challenging not because of its attacks but because of the enemies on the board, which that part is fine, but I feel like for it to be the final boss of the game, it needs more credit. With all that said, the game is still a good game that could use a bit more polishing.

When I downloaded this game, I played it for about six hours straight, because the initial game has lots of options for metaprogression which is one of my favorite part of any roguelite. However, as I went to bed, I started to feel that the game was too heavily based on randomness to really be worth sinking any more time into. I can't say what happened, but when I woke up the next morning, I saw through the matrix. I began to understand how to progress, how to avoid taking unnecessary risks, what types of decisions I could make to increase my chances of survival, etc. I ended up maxxing out all of the unlocks at about 14 hours. I set myself the final goal of getting a winning run with each of the characters, which I knocked out in another 7 hours or so. I will not play Sol Cesto anymore, but the 20 hours I had with this game were absolutely delightful. Yes, there are some valid complaints about the game: there is not much lore, some abilities are too much stronger than others, etc. But who cares? For a game you will play for hundreds of hours, those complaints matter because they means that runs can get repetitive and stale. For a game you intend to play for twenty hours, learning and finding the best strategy for each character is part of the fun! And by the time the game starts to get repetitive you have probably completed everything anyway and are ready to move onto other games. The gambling style nature of the gameplay is exciting, the luck mitigation elements are satisfying, the art is delightful, the metaprogression is pleasing and some hidden moments are hilarious. I highly recommend this game.

A surprisingly well made game with deep mechanics, unique art style and sound design, as well as some interesting worldbuilding and lore in the background. Core mechanics are very simple and easy to understand, with UI doing a great job at showing the player what is going on and what they are about to do with any given action. There are also some mechanics and interactions that aren't explicitly explained to the player (for example how different items may interact with certain abilities), so there are still ways to experiment with the game and it often pays off. The outcome of combat/exploration is largely luck based, but the game gives you many tools (items, abilities, modifiers, etc.) to sway the odds in your favor. Choices you make feel impactful and often need careful consideration and planning to give player the best chance of a favorable outcome. However, even the most optimal strategies often don't guarantee safety, but understanding the game and planning ahead allow you to deal with consequences of random failures... most of the time. You can always loose to shear bad luck, with minimal mistakes made in the run, which is an intended part of Sol Cesto experience. The game feels generally well balanced - different items all have their uses, each modifier can be helpful in some way (or detrimental, if chosen poorly) and heroes all have some strengths that make them viable. I do however think, that difficulty of different stages (or bioms) of the journey isn't scaled too well. Monsters and other hazards do get stronger as you progress, but the begging is still the most difficult and luck dependent part, where most runs die. With no modifiers and little money you are at the mercy of game's level generation, without strategies you usually depend on once you get some upgrades to help you. I really wish the early floors were a bit more forgiving, especially for the characters with lower hp. The art style is cartoony, with creatures ranging from cute to grotesque and simple objects like chests or spikes. Playable characters and few NPCs you may encounter all have unique designs, which establish their identities and roles in a world where dialogue and other information about them is scarce. The setting is based on dark ages and dark phantasy, which gives Sol Cesto a feeling and aesthetic similar to Dark Souls. Most elements of the world are bizzare end grotesque (like inserting new teeth into your jaw for modifiers), but there are some more whimsical scenes (like stumbling upon a calm water fountain in the forest and fishing out powerful upgrades). All in all nothing feels out of place, every detail of the art is polished to perfection and it is easily one of the most appealing aspects of the game. I recommend Sol Cesto to literally anyone who likes roguelike games and can handle some luck based gameplay.

I have played a few games in the vein of Pyrene that have more going for them in terms of visual flare than they do in terms of actual gameplay. the core loop of the game is fun, but the modifiers and lack of enemy / level diversity really hurt the replay value. The teeth in particular leave a lot to be desired imo, the "attraction" mechanic is interesting but the amount of control it actually gives you in a run is tiny. The teeth with "triggered" effects (ex. open a chest, disable a trap) are much more interesting but they are unreliable to activate, and even if you do manage to trigger your tooth there is no guarantee that you will be able to capitalize on that trigger. It causes the gameplay loop to boil down to "click on the lane with the highest percentage for a good outcome and pray" which makes the moment to moment gameplay very dull. Items are either difficult to utilize of they completely solve a problem for you, (the key item allows you to completely skip floors including bosses) and they're really expensive for what they do. The fact that your character can fall into a trap multiple times in a row is very frustrating, I really don't like games that make you collect 10,000 of their arbitrary currency before you can play the full game ( I do not have the free time nor desire to grind out every star). Overall I think the game needs more teeth with meaningful triggers, more ways to cope with bad luck or make actually impactful decisions, and more special enemies with actual interesting effects. OVERALL, if you're a gameplay andy I would skip, if you want to see the pretty pictures and you don't care about completing the game it could be for you. currently debating a refund.
